title: Which joint's torque limit sets how fast a stock humanoid can carry a load?
summary: The Menagerie G1 and H1 humanoids are re-scored on buildbot-carryphase's prescribed single-support carry step (990 cases: payload, step length, step time) with one joint group's torque limits multiplied by 2 or 4. For the G1 the waist pitch (50 N·m in the model) is the wall: doubling it alone lifts the heaviest feasible payload from 4 to 6 kg and the 4 kg speed from 0.10 to 0.20 m/s, while the arms, legs or ankles alone change nothing; all joints at 4× reach 10 kg. The H1 has no single bottleneck (hip pitch, then elbow): only scaling every joint helps. Best speed stays near 0.2 m/s because the gait is prescribed. Limits are the community Menagerie model's, scale factors are swept what-ifs (no actuator is claimed), payload steps are coarse, and no falls or energy are scored. Not a safety case.
lede: which joint's torque limit caps a stock humanoid's carrying? For the G1 it is the waist pitch: doubling it alone takes the heaviest feasible payload from 4 to 6 kg; the H1 has no single bottleneck.
why_standalone: A one-run buildbot project begun before the programme bar (2026-10-24) and merged minutes after it; the buildbot series has no programme proposal yet in research/PROGRAMMES.md.
